function.description: Send a GET request to a specified URL to retrieve all products and branches with triangulation runs in the latest 90 days. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to send the GET request to.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The MIME types that are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request as a dictionary of header names to header values.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

days.description: The number of days to look back for triangulation runs.

end_date.description: The end date for the data retrieval period, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'. If null, defaults to the current date.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the request.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to a certificate file to verify the peer.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names to cookie values.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary mapping protocol names to URLs of the proxies.

stream.description: If true, the response should be streamed; otherwise, the response will be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not.

message.content:
**Triangulation Metrics** refers to a set of quantitative measures used to evaluate the quality, accuracy, and reliability of triangulation results in various contexts—such as geospatial mapping, computer vision, robotics, or any system that relies on triangulating positions or features from multiple observations.

Key aspects typically covered by triangulation metrics include:

| Metric | What it Measures | Typical Use |
|--------|------------------|-------------|
| **Accuracy** | Difference between the estimated position and the true (ground‑truth) position. | Assessing how close the triangulated point is to its real location. |
| **Precision** | Variability of repeated triangulations under identical conditions. | Evaluating consistency across multiple runs. |
| **Uncertainty / Confidence Interval** | Statistical bounds (e.g., 95% CI) around the estimated point. | Providing a probabilistic sense of reliability. |
| **Error Ellipse / Covariance Matrix** | Shape and orientation of the error distribution. | Visualizing directional uncertainty. |
| **Signal‑to‑Noise Ratio (SNR)** | Strength of the signal relative to background noise. | Gauging measurement quality. |
| **Baseline Length / Geometry Factor** | Distance between observation points or angular spread. | Influencing the robustness of triangulation. |
| **Redundancy / Over‑determination** | Number of independent measurements beyond the minimum required. | Enhancing solution stability. |
| **Residuals / Goodness‑of‑Fit** | Sum of squared differences between observed and predicted values. | Checking model adequacy. |
| **Computational Efficiency** | Time or resources needed to compute triangulation. | Optimizing real‑time systems. |

In practice, a triangulation system might report a combination of these metrics to give stakeholders a comprehensive view of performance. For example, a GPS receiver might provide an estimated position along with a 95 % confidence ellipse, while a photogrammetry pipeline might output residuals and a covariance matrix for each reconstructed point.
